name: browser-app-builder
description: Guide a student from local setup to a planned, tested browser app and GitHub Pages publication, with bundled Campus Designer styling.

interface.shortDescription: Plan, build, evaluate, and publish a browser app. No coding experience is required.
interface.longDescription: Turn a problem you understand into a self-contained browser application, with a saved plan, local revision history, calculation evidence, and GitHub Pages publication. Your agent handles the files and commands; you make the product and model decisions. Five workflow skills select from sixteen approved library skills for charts, diagrams, timelines, schedules, tables, React controls, slides, animation, CSV, data transformation, statistics, and reproducible randomness. Library apps use an agent-managed Node/npm/Vite build; simple apps can still use native browser features without Node. Bundled Campus Designer guidance and library-specific themes provide consistent Duke colors and typography. The live examples include independently reviewed library applications and the earlier version 0.1.1 plain-app trials, all using simulated planning conversations and synthetic data. Local mapping, bounded SQL exploration and worker-based optimization are approved for the reviewed configurations.
defaultPrompt: Use setup-browser-app to prepare this folder.
Use plan-browser-app to help me plan a pricing scenario calculator.
Use build-browser-app to implement the agreed PLAN.md.
Use evaluate-browser-app to check the calculations with me and record the evidence.
Use deploy-browser-app to help me publish the evaluated app on GitHub Pages.
Help me plan an interactive analytical presentation with local pricing scenarios.
Help me plan an editable process diagram.
Help me plan a dashboard that imports a local synthetic CSV.

io.github.jordanmeyer.label: Pilot candidate · Instructor-built
io.github.jordanmeyer.audience: MBA students building a self-contained decision tool, dashboard, or simulation with an agent.

results.label: Passing browser checks across nine revised examples
Earlier plain-app trials published and verified live
Revised apps independently reviewed and verified live

io.github.jordanmeyer.method: Nine original applications were built from recorded simulated planning conversations on a configured Mac, then revised against the 0.2.3 guidance. Three developers worked in parallel; independent review checked models, useful default scenarios, interaction and production output before publication. The revised browser suites total 285 passing checks. Exact-commit GitHub Actions deployments and live known-answer interactions were verified for all nine, including returning-browser reloads. Revisions added clearer decision tradeoffs, consistent local typography, accessible alternatives to dense widgets, explicit pending states and public build stories. Review caught stale restored controls, chart and table layout issues, rank explanations and presentation initialization timing. Original campaign evidence and the earlier 0.1.1 plain-app trials remain separate historical records. These are maintainer-run simulations, not student outcomes or automatic ChatGPT Work routing trials. The evidence record preserves source checkpoints, failures, corrections, review verdicts and deployment results.
io.github.jordanmeyer.limits: Self-contained apps use bundled public/synthetic data or locally selected files. No backends, logins, external runtime APIs, remote AI, analytics, secret keys or remote fonts/scripts. Managed builds require compatible Node/npm and host file, shell and browser capabilities. Library approval covers the recorded versions/configurations, not arbitrary combinations. Work routing, clean-machine macOS/Windows and novice-student usability remain unverified. Browser checks do not certify a business model or full accessibility.
